findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the release to the hand-checked candidate: create the bump worktree from d6ba771aabac (or assert origin/main == d6ba771aabac first). After Submit, confirm the merge SHA's parent is d6ba771aabac. Immediately before `gh workflow run`, confirm origin/main HEAD == the recorded merge SHA, and stop to re-check if either assertion fails.
evidence: Plan: 'The release candidate is origin/main `d6ba771aabac`, hand-checked on 2026-11-13'
Plan step 1: 'In a fresh worktree at origin/main' (no SHA pin)
docs/releasing.md §2: the workflow runs from the `main` ref, and the ancestry guard only checks reachability from origin/main, not equality with a reviewed candidate
findings.finding: The plan validates a specific candidate (origin/main d6ba771aabac, hand-checked on 2026-11-13) but never ties the release to that commit. The bump worktree is cut from whatever 'origin/main' is at the time, and `release.yml --ref main` builds whatever main HEAD is at dispatch. Any change that lands between the hand-check, the bump branch, Gerrit submit and dispatch would be published without the 7 functional checks and the wheel smoke test, and would be missing from the CHANGELOG reconciled against `git log v0.15.1..HEAD`. This is a check-then-act gap: what was checked is not what gets released.
findings.location: Context / Problem ('release candidate is origin/main d6ba771aabac'); Approach step 1 ('In a fresh worktree at origin/main'); Approach step 3 (dispatch --ref main)
scenarios: Another Gerrit change is submitted to main after the 2026-11-13 hand-check but before the bump worktree is created: the release ships it untested, and the CHANGELOG range differs from what was curated.
Main moves between the bump commit's push and its Submit: Gerrit rebases or merges, so the merge SHA's parent is no longer d6ba771, and an unrelated commit sits between the candidate and the release.
A change lands after the bump is submitted but before `gh workflow run`: the release builds main HEAD, which is not the recorded merge SHA.
findings.suggested_fix: Step 1: `git fetch origin && test "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" = d6ba771aabac… && git worktree add ../rel-0.16.0 d6ba771aabac`. After Submit, record the merge SHA and check `git rev-parse <merge>^` == d6ba771aabac. Step 3: before dispatch, `git fetch origin && test "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" = <merge-sha>`. Then check that the run's headSha (from `gh run view $RUN --json headSha`) equals <merge-sha>.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the full approval body (`environment_ids`, `state: "approved"`, `comment`) and how `$RUN` and the pypi environment id are derived.
evidence: "POST repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments with a JSON `--input` body (`environment_ids` integer array)"
findings.finding: Step 4's pending-deployments API body names only `environment_ids`. GitHub's 'Review pending deployments for a workflow run' endpoint also requires `state` ("approved") and `comment`. The step also does not say how `$RUN` and the environment id are obtained.

findings.suggested_fix: RUN=$(gh run list --workflow release.yml --repo navapbc/rebar --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId'); ENV_ID=$(gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments -q '.[] | select(.environment.name=="pypi") | .environment.id'); echo "{\"environment_ids\":[$ENV_ID],\"state\":\"approved\",\"comment\":\"Release 0.16.0\"}" | gh api -X POST repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments --input -

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the GitHub Release AC's verify step one structured check asserting tag_name==v0.16.0 on /releases/latest and both asset files are present.

"instrument=live-call — gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/releases/latest"
findings.finding: The GitHub Release AC text and its instrument name different checks. The text says `gh release view v0.16.0`; the provenance says `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/releases/latest`. Neither has a structured assertion for 'marked Latest' or for the attached wheel and sdist (cardinality and names).
scenarios: The release exists but is not Latest, or only the sdist uploaded, and a prose read of `gh release view` is taken as a pass.
findings.suggested_fix: gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/releases/latest | jq -e '.tag_name=="v0.16.0" and ([.assets[].name | select(test("^nava_rebar-0\\.16\\.0(-py3-none-any\\.whl|\\.tar\\.gz)$"))] | length)==2'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the registry and Homebrew checks with anchored structured assertions (jq on the registry version; decoded formula grep for the exact 0.16.0 sdist URL).
evidence: "`curl -s \"https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.navapbc/rebar\"` lists version 0.16.0"
"points at the 0.16.0 sdist (`gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb`)"
findings.finding: The MCP Registry and Homebrew ACs use prose-level checks. Search results can list several versions, so 'lists version 0.16.0' is unanchored. The contents API returns base64 content, which must be decoded before asserting the sdist URL.
scenarios: The registry still marks 0.15.1 as latest, or a stale formula is accepted by eyeballing encoded output.
findings.suggested_fix: curl -s '…/v0/servers?search=io.github.navapbc/rebar' | jq -e '[.servers[] | (.server.version // .version)] | index("0.16.0")'; gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb -q .content | base64 -d | grep -E 'nava_rebar-0\.16\.0\.tar\.gz'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 0.16.0 Added entries with CHANGELOG [0.15.1]. Present the agentic engine implementation, the permanence of `[verify] plan_review_engine`, and the new `engine` fields on plan_review_status and attestations as changes to the 0.15.1 surface, and state that the 0.15.1 'agentic not implemented yet' INDETERMINATE behaviour is replaced.
evidence: Plan: 'Main since v0.15.1 … carries the implemented `agentic` plan-review engine (ADR 0123): `rebar review-plan --engine`, an optional `engine` parameter on the MCP … tools, … and `[verify] plan_review_engine` as a permanent setting.'

CHANGELOG.md:43–47 under '## [0.15.1] - 2026-11-11' / '### Added': 'ADR 0123: selectable plan-review engine, and the `[verify] plan_review_engine` setting (`pipeline`, the default, or `agentic`). An explicit per-call engine argument overrides the setting. The `agentic` engine is not implemented yet…'
docs/release-notes.md has no plan_review_engine/agentic entry (searching it for 'engine' turns up only unrelated entries), so the contract note the plan proposes would be the first one
findings.finding: The Context says main since v0.15.1 'carries' `rebar review-plan --engine`, the MCP `engine` parameter and `[verify] plan_review_engine`. The shipped CHANGELOG says otherwise: its [0.15.1] section already lists, under Added, 'ADR 0123: selectable plan-review engine, and the `[verify] plan_review_engine` setting … An explicit per-call engine argument overrides the setting', and notes that the agentic engine was not implemented yet. So the setting and the per-call argument were already released. What is new in 0.16.0 is the agentic implementation, the permanence ruling and the status/attestation `engine` fields. The plan's Added entries rest on this framing, so they risk re-announcing surface that already shipped and never retracting the 0.15.1 'not implemented yet' note.
findings.location: Context / Problem — engine-surface sentence; Approach step 1 CHANGELOG 'Added/Fixed entries'
scenarios: The 0.16.0 Added section lists `[verify] plan_review_engine` and the per-call engine argument as new, even though 0.15.1 users already had them. Or a reconciliation against git log silently drops them, and 0.16.0 never says the 0.15.1 'agentic not implemented' caveat no longer applies.
findings.suggested_fix: In the CHANGELOG step, add: 'Do not re-list the `[verify] plan_review_engine` key or the per-call engine argument as new (both are in [0.15.1] Added). Under Added/Changed, record that the `agentic` engine is now implemented (no longer an unsigned INDETERMINATE), that the key is permanent per ADR 0123, and that `engine` is new on plan_review_status and agentic attestations.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before approving, resolve $RUN as the release.yml workflow_dispatch run whose headSha equals the recorded merge SHA and that started after this session's dispatch. Record that id, and approve only that run.
evidence: Plan step 4: 'Approve the pending `pypi` deployment via `POST repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments`' ($RUN is never defined)
docs/releasing.md §2: `RUN=$(gh run list --workflow=release.yml --event=workflow_dispatch -L1 ...)`, which takes the newest run with no check of its SHA or inputs
findings.finding: Step 4 approves `actions/runs/$RUN/pending_deployments`, but the plan never says how $RUN is obtained or confirmed to be the 0.16.0 dispatch. The runbook takes the newest workflow_dispatch run (`gh run list ... -L1`). If two dispatches overlap, or an earlier run is still waiting, that picks the wrong run and the approval releases the publish job of a different run.
findings.location: Approach steps 3–4; AC '[non-codebase] release.yml run for 0.16.0 completes successfully (run id recorded)'
scenarios: A stale run dispatched earlier is still waiting at the pypi environment, so `-L1` resolves to the wrong run and the approval publishes something other than the 0.16.0 merge SHA.
The run list has not refreshed yet when the RUN lookup executes immediately after dispatch.
findings.suggested_fix: `RUN=$(gh run list --workflow=release.yml --event=workflow_dispatch --json databaseId,headSha,createdAt -q '[.[] | select(.headSha=="<merge-sha>")][0].databaseId')`, then confirm with `gh run view $RUN --json headSha,status` before the POST.
